items.title: Bob Cranshaw interviewed by Michael Woods, New York City, New York, October 18, 1995
items.q: So working with a lot of piano players like Monty Alexander and working with Erroll Garner and people like that who play by ear.

ctx.x: Yeah. But for me, I think it enabled me to be able to do a lot of things you know? Because I can go out on a job when well I’ve heard the music or whatever. I’m never

frightened as to what, you know, music in front of you, then that’s another story because it’s there so you don’t have a chance to do you know those things. And it took me a long time to really learn to read because I had depended upon my ear for so many years that it took again, a lot of practice to learn to read. But I was determined that I was going to win that battle also. And I did. But the ear part has just helped me, especially with the jazz things. I just, again, I don’t, I play what I hear. I know the…
So in other words, you can go all three ways. If they give you notes, if they give you changes, or if they just ask you to hear the forms.
